source_text:
Ὁ δὲ
καταγνοὺς αὐτῶν, ἐδήλωσεν αὐτοῖς λέγων, ὅτι Φανεροί ἐστε ἀμελοῦντες τὰς ἄλλας
ὥρας τῆς ἡμέρας ἀργοῦντες ἀπὸ τῆς εὐχῆς. ∆εῖ γὰρ τὸν ἀληθινὸν μοναχὸν
ἀδιαλείπτως ἔχειν τὴν εὐχὴν καὶ τὴν ψαλμῳδίαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
δʹ. Ἔπεμψέ ποτε ὁ ἅγιος Ἐπιφάνιος πρὸς τὸν ἀββᾶν Ἱλαρίωνα, παρακαλῶν
αὐτὸν, καὶ λέγων· ∆εῦρο, ἴδωμεν ἑαυτοὺς πρὸ τοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος·
καὶ παραγενομένου αὐτοῦ, ἐχάρησαν μετ' ἀλλήλων. Ἐσθιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν, ἠνέχθη
πετεινόν. Καὶ λαβὼν ὁ ἐπίσκοπος ἔδωκε τῷ ἀββᾷ Ἱλαρίωνι. Καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ γέρων·
Συγχώρησόν μοι, ὅτι ἐξ οὗ ἔλαβον τὸ σχῆμα, οὐκ ἔφαγον θῦμα. Καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ
ἐπίσκοπος· Ἐγὼ δὲ ἐξ οὗ ἔλαβον τὸ σχῆμα, οὐκ ἀφῆκά τινα κοιμηθῆναι ἔχοντα κατ'
ἐμοῦ, οὐδὲ ἐγὼ ἐκοιμήθην ἔχων κατὰ τινός. Καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ γέρων· Συγχώρησόν
μοι, ὅτι ἡ σὴ πολιτεία μείζων ἐστὶ τῆς ἐμῆς.
εʹ. Ὁ αὐτὸς ἔλεγεν, ὅτι ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ Χριστοῦ Μελχισεδὲκ, τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν
Ἰουδαίων εὐλόγησε τὸν Ἀβραάμ· πολλῷ πλέον αὐτὴ ἡ ἀλήθεια ὁ Χριστὸς, εὐλογεῖ
καὶ ἁγιάζει πάντας τοὺς πιστεύοντας εἰς αὐτόν.
ς ʹ.
thought_title: Epiphanius rebukes his monks and exchanges ascetic boasts with Hilarion
orientation: Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus, has just received a report from his monastery in Palestine that the monks keep only the third, sixth, and ninth hours of prayer.
pass_a_gloss: But he, having condemned them, made clear to them saying, that "You are manifest neglecting the other hours of the day, being idle from prayer. For it is necessary [for] the true monk unceasingly to have the prayer and the psalmody in his heart." 4. [He] sent once the holy Epiphanius to the abba Hilarion, urging him, and saying: "Come, let us see each other before [the] going out [of] us from the body"; and [when] he had arrived, they rejoiced with each other. [While] they were eating, [there] was brought a bird. And [having] taken [it] the bishop gave [it] to the abba Hilarion. And says to him the old man: "Forgive me, because from [the time] when I took the habit, I have not eaten [anything] slain." And says to him the bishop: "But I, from [the time] when I took the habit, have not let anyone go to sleep having [anything] against me, nor did I go to sleep having [anything] against anyone." And says to him the old man: "Forgive me, because your way of life is greater than mine." 5. The same one said, that "The image of Christ [is] Melchizedek; the root of the Jews blessed Abraham; much more [does] the truth itself, Christ, bless and sanctify all those believing in him." 6.

choices.why: The participle carries a judicial force of disapproval, not merely 'discerning' or 'noticing'; it sets up the rebuke that follows.
The construction with ἀπό marks separation from prayer as the sphere of their idleness; 'idle from prayer' preserves the Greek idiom and the force of the accusation.

choices.term: ∆εῖ γὰρ τὸν ἀληθινὸν μοναχὸν ἀδιαλείπτως ἔχειν τὴν εὐχὴν καὶ τὴν ψαλμῳδίαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ
choices.english: For the true monk must have prayer and psalmody unceasingly in his heart
choices.why: The impersonal δεῖ expresses necessity; 'must' is the natural English equivalent. 'True monk' renders ἀληθινὸν μοναχόν, contrasting with the monks who only keep three hours.
rejected: it is necessary for the true monk to have
the true monk ought to have

choices.term: οὐκ ἀφῆκά τινα κοιμηθῆναι ἔχοντα κατ' ἐμοῦ
choices.english: I have not let anyone go to sleep holding anything against me
choices.why: The idiom ἔχοντα κατά τινος means holding a grievance; 'holding anything against me' captures the interpersonal force of the boast.

choices.english: Melchizedek is an image of Christ
choices.why: The word order places the predicate first; rendering it as an equative clause makes the theological claim clear in English.

choices.term: τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων εὐλόγησε τὸν Ἀβραάμ
choices.english: the root of the Jews blessed Abraham
choices.why: The accusative 'the root of the Jews' is in apposition to Melchizedek; keeping it as a noun phrase preserves the compressed syntax of the saying.
rejected: he blessed Abraham, the root of the Jews
as the root of the Jews he blessed Abraham

pass_b_english: But he condemned them and made it clear to them, saying: "It is obvious that you are neglecting the other hours of the day, being idle from prayer. For the true monk must have prayer and psalmody unceasingly in his heart."

Once holy Epiphanius sent to Abba Hilarion, urging him and saying: "Come, let us see each other before we depart from the body." And when he arrived, they rejoiced with one another. While they were eating, a bird was brought in. The bishop took it and gave it to Abba Hilarion. The old man says to him: "Forgive me, for since I received the habit I have not eaten sacrificial meat." The bishop says to him: "But I, since I received the habit, have not let anyone go to sleep holding anything against me, nor have I gone to sleep holding anything against anyone." The old man says to him: "Forgive me, for your way of life is greater than mine."
The same one said that Melchizedek is an image of Christ: he blessed Abraham, the root of the Jews. How much more does the truth itself, Christ, bless and sanctify all who believe in him.

problems.why: τὴν ῥίζαν is accusative object of εὐλόγησε, not 'root of the Jews'; it means 'blessed the root of the Jews,' i.e., Abraham as ancestor.
problems.fix: he blessed the root of the Jews, Abraham
problems.ruling: τὴν ῥίζαν is accusative object of εὐλόγησε: 'blessed the root of the Jews' (Abraham), not 'the root of the Jews blessed Abraham.'

edits.old: the root of the Jews blessed Abraham
edits.new: he blessed the root of the Jews, Abraham

fixed: Changed 'the root of the Jews blessed Abraham' to 'he blessed the root of the Jews, Abraham' because in the source 'τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων' is the accusative object of 'εὐλόγησε', meaning Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who is the root of the Jews.

problems.why: θῦμα specifically means sacrificial victim/sacrifice, not merely 'anything slain'—Hilarion avoids sacrificial meat, not all slaughtered animals.
problems.ruling: θῦμα means sacrificial victim, not 'anything slain.' Hilarion refuses sacrificial meat specifically, not all meat.

edits.old: I have not eaten anything slain
edits.new: I have not eaten sacrificial meat

fixed: Changed 'anything slain' to 'sacrificial meat' because θῦμα means sacrificial victim, not merely slaughtered animal.

problems.quote: he blessed the root of the Jews, Abraham
problems.source_quote: τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων εὐλόγησε τὸν Ἀβραάμ
problems.why: Abraham is the root of the Jews, not the object blessed separately. The syntax says he blessed Abraham, the root of the Jews.
problems.fix: he blessed Abraham, the root of the Jews
problems.ruling: Greek has accusative τὸν Ἀβραάμ as object of εὐλόγησε; τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων is apposition, not separate object. English 'blessed the root of the Jews, Abraham' makes two objects, misrepresenting syntax.

edits.old: he blessed the root of the Jews, Abraham
edits.new: he blessed Abraham, the root of the Jews

fixed: Corrected: the source syntax is 'τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων εὐλόγησε τὸν Ἀβραάμ', where 'τὸν Ἀβραάμ' is the direct object of 'εὐλόγησε' and 'τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων' is in apposition to Abraham.

last_rejected.quote: The old man says to him
last_rejected.why: English present tense hides that Hilarion spoke in the past narrative.
last_rejected.fix: The old man said to him
last_rejected.ruling: Greek λέγει is present tense; English 'says' matches it. Historical present is standard narrative style.

last_rejected.why: English present tense hides that Epiphanius spoke in the past narrative.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek λέγει is present tense; English 'says' faithfully renders it. Historical present is normal in such texts.

last_rejected.why: English present tense hides that Hilarion spoke in the past narrative.
last_rejected.fix: The old man said to him
last_rejected.ruling: Greek λέγει is present tense; English 'says' matches exactly. Historical present is a valid rendering choice.
καταγνοὺς can mean 'condemned' (LSJ s.v. καταγινώσκω II); within normal range, not a meaning change.
